decks.notes: The primary strategy of this deck is to disrupt your opponent's plays through countermagic and removal spells while generating card advantage. Using powerful cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Wasteland, the deck aims to control the board and outvalue the opponent. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value by allowing you to continually reuse low-cost permanents. By carefully managing resources and utilizing cards like Dig Through Time and Ancestral Recall, this Esper Control deck aims to grind out victories through careful planning and strategic play.

The deck revolves around utilizing powerful artifacts like Coveted Jewel, The One Ring, and Time Vault to generate mana and draw cards quickly. By combining cards like Mishra's Workshop, Grim Monolith, and Paradoxical Outcome, the deck aims to assemble its combo pieces efficiently while controlling the opponent with cards like Force of Will and Sink into Stupor. With access to cards like Tinker and Karn, the Great Creator, the deck can further access its powerful artifacts and disrupt the opponent's game plan. The ultimate goal is to generate a massive advantage and overwhelm the opponent with powerful artifacts and combo plays.

This Vintage MUD Aggro deck focuses on accelerating mana production using Mishra's Workshop and Moxen to quickly cast powerful artifacts like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Stonecoil Serpent. It also aims to disrupt opponents' strategies by utilizing cards like Trinisphere, Null Rod, and Sphere of Resistance, while maintaining control of the board with cards like Strip Mine and Ghost Quarter. The deck's high artifact count synergizes well with cards like Karn, the Great Creator and Inventors' Fair, allowing for versatile gameplay and adaptability in different matchups.

This deck focuses on quickly ramping up mana using artifact ramp cards like Moxen, Sol Ring, and Mana Vault to get out powerful threats like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge. The deck also utilizes cards like Manifold Key and Nettlecyst to pump up creatures like Glaring Fleshraker and Patchwork Automaton, allowing for aggressive plays and quick wins. With additional support cards like Sensei's Divining Top and Lodestone Golem, this deck aims to overwhelm the opponent's resources and secure victory through sheer speed and efficiency in Vintage 1 vs 1 matches.

The deck focuses on utilizing powerful artifact cards like Coveted Jewel, Time Vault, and The One Ring to generate immense value and win the game through a powerful combo. It also includes cards like Tinker, Paradoxical Outcome, and Karn, the Great Creator to search for or manipulate key pieces of the combo. The deck also includes disruption elements like Force of Will and Trinisphere to control the game and protect its win condition. With a mix of ramp, card draw, and combo pieces, the deck aims to quickly assemble its combo and overwhelm the opponent.

This Dimir Control deck aims to control the game through counterspells and removal, using cards like Force of Will, Fatal Push, and Spell Pierce to disrupt the opponent's game plan. It also utilizes card draw and library manipulation with Ancestral Recall, Brainstorm, and Gitaxian Probe to ensure consistency and card advantage. The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy while setting up its own win conditions, potentially utilizing Lórien Revealed and Orcish Bowmasters to gain incremental advantage and eventually overwhelm the opponent.

This aggro MUD deck focuses on disrupting the opponent with cards like Sphere of Resistance, Thorn of Amethyst, and Crucible of Worlds, while ramping up quickly with Mishra's Workshop and fast mana artifacts. Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Mystic Forge provide card advantage and versatility, while Nettlecyst and Stonecoil Serpent offer threats that are difficult to deal with. Karn, the Great Creator acts as a versatile toolbox, while Null Rod and Strip Mine shut down opposing strategies. The deck aims to overpower the opponent quickly and efficiently, using a variety of disruptive and powerful artifacts.

This deck's strategy revolves around utilizing powerful artifact creatures and mana acceleration to quickly overwhelm the opponent. With access to powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Time Vault, as well as synergies with cards like Manifold Key and Nettlecyst, the deck can generate explosive plays early in the game. By leveraging the mana base provided by cards like Mishra's Workshop and Ancient Tomb, the deck can deploy threats quickly and efficiently, pressuring the opponent and ending the game before they have a chance to stabilize.

The deck focuses on controlling the opponent's game plan by disrupting their threats with counter spells, removal, and land destruction. It also utilizes card draw and tutors to find key cards and maintain card advantage. The inclusion of Lurrus as a companion allows for additional value by recurring cheap permanents from the graveyard. With a mix of efficient removal spells, counterspells, and card advantage engines, the deck aims to grind out a win by limiting the opponent's resources and slowly progressing its own game plan.

The deck utilizes a combination of disruptive cards like Collector Ouphe and Force of Will, along with efficient threats like Deathrite Shaman and Oko, Thief of Crowns to control the board and pressure the opponent. It also includes card advantage and selection tools like Ancestral Recall and Brainstorm to maintain consistency and tempo. The mana base is designed to support the deck's color requirements while also including powerful utility lands like Wasteland and Boseiju, Who Endures. Overall, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while advancing its own through a mix of aggression and control.

This deck focuses on locking down the opponent's resources while quickly deploying powerful threats. It utilizes artifact synergies to generate mana and disrupt the opponent's strategy, with cards like Mishra's Workshop, Null Rod, and Sphere of Resistance. The deck also takes advantage of powerful artifacts like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Mystic Forge to generate card advantage and close out the game. The goal is to overwhelm the opponent with efficient threats and resource denial, leading to a quick victory in the early game.

The deck focuses on fast-paced aggression using powerful merfolk creatures and disruption spells to control the game. The key strategy is to use mana acceleration cards like Moxen to play threats ahead of curve, while also having access to countermagic to protect your creatures or disrupt the opponent's game plan. With powerful disruptive creatures like Hullbreacher and Tishana's Tidebinder, along with efficient beaters like Merrow Reejerey, the deck aims to win quickly by overwhelming the opponent with a combination of control elements and aggressive creatures.

Utilize card advantage, counterspells, and disruptive creatures to control the game and slow down the opponent's strategy. By leveraging Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion, recurring cheap threats and value spells to outvalue the opponent while disrupting their game plan. With a mix of powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time, along with efficient removal like Swords to Plowshares, the deck aims to stay ahead in resources and grind out the game at a pace that best suits the player's strategy.

This deck focuses on utilizing the powerful draw engine of Paradoxical Outcome to generate card advantage and mana acceleration, enabling explosive combo plays. By efficiently cycling through artifacts and leveraging mana rocks, the deck aims to generate large amounts of mana to cast key spells like Ancestral Recall and Time Walk. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds resilience and flexibility to the deck's game plan, making it able to withstand disruption and outvalue opponents in longer games.

The key focus of this deck is to quickly assemble the necessary cards for a game-winning combo using Doomsday. The deck includes a variety of card draw and manipulation spells, such as Ponder, Preordain, and Brainstorm, to dig for key pieces like Thassa's Oracle and Doomsday. The deck also includes disruption cards like Force of Will and Duress to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's game plan. With the ability to quickly and efficiently set up the combo, this deck aims to win the game in a single explosive turn.

The deck focuses on deploying hatebears to disrupt the opponent's game plan while putting pressure on them with aggressive creatures. The deck utilizes mana denial tactics such as Wasteland and Chalice of the Void, along with disruptive creatures like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex. Additionally, the deck includes powerful cards like Black Lotus and Moxen to ramp out threats quickly. With a mix of hate cards, aggressive creatures, and mana acceleration, this deck aims to control the board and overwhelm the opponent in a Vintage 1 vs 1 format.
